OH-SP.adSrc: Statehouse News Bureau / WVXU (Sarah Donaldson, Oct 9, 2026) citing AdImpact
OH-SP.headline: The most expensive race of 2026
OH-SP.story: About $250M had been spent through Sept 30, with about $140M more reserved for October and November (AdImpact via Statehouse News Bureau). Other tallies differ by basis, from $197M by Sept 22 (Washington Post) to $298M (Reuters, Sept 18). No dollar split by party was found; AdImpact data show Republicans generally outspending Democrats (Statehouse News Bureau, Oct 9), and Brown’s campaign was the race’s top single advertiser at about $37.5M, with One Nation, a nonprofit allied with Senate Republicans, close behind (AdImpact via Deseret News). Issue-ad campaigns by nonprofits are not in the flow chart: One Nation’s amount was not given, and three environmental groups announced $9M of FirstEnergy ads aimed at Husted that E&E News calls “not explicitly an election ad.”

TX-S.adBasis: general election through Sept 30; the sides come from Oct 5 reports (Lone Star Rising’s from Sept 17), so they add to more than the total
TX-S.story: Talarico’s campaign has far outspent Paxton’s on ads, but Republicans spent $122M on ads in September, all but $1.2M of it from outside groups, and more than 98% of the $205M-plus in general-election outside spending backed Paxton (Texas Tribune, Oct 1). Through September, Republicans had 72% of broadcast ad dollars but 54% of the ratings points those dollars bought (AdImpact).

ME-S.story: Republicans led TV spending after Jackson’s nomination, $82.1M to $55.5M, but Democrats paid about $263 per rating point to Republicans’ $323, and reservations after Sept 15 narrowed the Republican edge in airtime to 7% (AdImpact via the Bangor Daily News). Graham Platner won the June 9 primary but withdrew; Troy Jackson was nominated at the July 25 state convention.

MI-S.adBasis: spent to about Oct 1; $65M more reserved
MI-S.story: More than $205M had been disclosed in the race, about $157M of it from outside groups, primary included (Bridge Michigan, Oct 2). AIPAC’s United Democracy Project spent about $20.1M against El-Sayed in the August primary (Newsweek, citing FEC filings) but reported no general-election spending.

NC-S.story: Senate Leadership Fund pledged $71M in April, spent more than $30M, then pulled its remaining North Carolina reservations on Oct 2; The New York Times reported them canceled, while AP and CBS called it a pause. Old North Action cut $6.5M of its October reservations, and WinSenate trimmed $1.1M but still had $18.8M scheduled as of Oct 8. In September, Republicans outspent Democrats on ads $53M to $44M (AdImpact via Axios Raleigh).

IA-S.adSrc: Iowa Capital Dispatch via News From The States (Oct 7, 2026)
IA-S.story: An open seat: Sen. Joni Ernst is retiring. Senate Majority PAC has committed more than $30M to Iowa TV, against a $29M Senate Leadership Fund reservation and $11M planned by One Nation. Ad spending passed $90M by the end of September (Iowa Capital Dispatch, citing the Washington Post).

AK-S.story: Of more than $31M in independent spending since the Aug 18 primary, groups backing Sullivan outspent those backing Peltola by nearly $7M (Alaska Public Media, Oct 2). The NRSC asked donors for an extra $1.2M for Alaska (Axios).

NH-S.adSrc: New Hampshire Bulletin via News From The States, 2026-09-14
NH-S.story: Republicans led on TV, $27M to $15.9M, as of Sept 14 (AdImpact via New Hampshire Bulletin). About 81% of Pappas’s and 86% of Sununu’s itemized donations in their latest reports came from out of state (OpenSecrets). No ad from Sununu’s own campaign was found; Punchbowl reported that the NRSC was running joint ads for him.

OH-GOV.adSrc: Voz (Joaquín Núñez, Sept 23, 2026) citing the Washington Post / AdImpact
OH-GOV.headline: Ramaswamy’s side outspent Acton’s more than 3 to 1 (NYT, Oct 5)
OH-GOV.story: Billionaires had given V-PAC $37M, more than 88% of its money, by mid-2026 (Ohio Capital Journal). The DGA-backed Ohioans for Lower Costs released its first ads for Acton on Aug 19 and booked TV time from Sept 8 (WVXU); its spending has not been disclosed. Candidate figures come from Ohio Secretary of State filings, not the FEC.

GA-S.story: Ossoff held a large cash edge at June 30, $42.6M to Collins’s $2.1M (FEC). Republican groups vowed about $60M, but less had materialized by mid-September (Atlanta Journal-Constitution), and Georgia was the only competitive Senate race where Republicans were not outspending Democrats on September ads (Axios, via the AJC). Senate Majority PAC has reserved $20M but had announced no Georgia ads on its website as of Oct 12.

MN-S.story: Little outside money so far: outside groups had not stepped in as of late September, and both campaigns had bought TV time around news and football (MPR, Sept 21). In the DFL primary, Craig outspent Flanagan on ads $9.6M to $1.9M (AdImpact).

SENATE.adBasis: AdImpact projection for all Senate races, 2025–26
SENATE.label: Senate control (all Senate races)
SENATE.story: Senate Leadership Fund, Senate Majority PAC and America PAC file quarterly, so their July–September money appears with the Oct 15 reports. Entering July, Democratic candidates in seven key races held $74.7M in cash to Republicans’ $36.8M, while conservative super PACs outspent Democratic ones $310M to $174M from Labor Day to Sept 25 (CNBC).

HOUSE.adBasis: AdImpact projection for all House races, 2025–26
HOUSE.label: House control (all House races)
HOUSE.story: Through Aug 31 the DCCC had out-raised the NRCC by about $0.9M this cycle, but the NRCC held about $13M more cash (FEC). House Majority PAC had $135.2M on hand at Aug 31; Congressional Leadership Fund’s last filed figure was $141.8M at June 30. House Majority PAC cut some planned buys in Nebraska’s 2nd and California’s 48th, and CLF was reported to be pulling out of Nebraska (Deseret News, Oct 6).

FL-25.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day
FL-25.outNote: Defending Our Values PAC has reported $857,426 backing Singer and Think Big $321,574 backing Moskowitz, cycle to date (FEC, via the Transformer tracker). House Majority PAC added nearly $5M in the Miami and West Palm Beach markets, not specific to this district.
FL-25.story: A newly redrawn seat that Trump won 54% to 45% inside the new lines. First in AdImpact spending among House races from Aug 1 (Punchbowl, Oct 6); spending to date rose from $8.4M to $14M in the week ending Oct 6 (Washington Post).

NC-01.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day
NC-01.outNote: Congressional Leadership Fund reserved nearly $10M (The Center Square, undated), and a nonprofit, apparently American Action Network, bought $1.3M of ads against Davis. Democratic groups’ amounts were not found.
NC-01.story: Second in AdImpact House spending from Aug 1 (Punchbowl, Oct 6). Davis had about twice Buckhout’s cash at June 30, $3.57M to $1.83M (FEC).

IA-01.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day
IA-01.headline: The most expensive House race of the cycle, primaries included (AdImpact via WKAR)
IA-01.outNote: American Action Network: more than $1M across Iowa’s 1st and 3rd Districts. Other groups’ amounts were not found.
IA-01.story: Miller-Meeks won in 2024 by 799 votes. Third in AdImpact spending from Aug 1 but first for the whole cycle; about 98% of the money through May 10 came from outside groups (Wesleyan Media Project).

MI-07.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day; the split by side covers a window not stated and adds to $32.6M
MI-07.headline: Second only to Iowa’s 1st this cycle, primaries included: $51.5M (AdImpact via WKAR)
MI-07.outBasis: House Majority PAC and Congressional Leadership Fund ad spending this cycle (AdImpact via WKAR)
MI-07.story: Democrats lead for the cycle because of their contested primary, while the later-window split shows Republicans slightly ahead (Punchbowl). More than $39M of broadcast TV was booked in the Lansing–Jackson market by late September (WKAR).

NY-17.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day; split from Sept 1
NY-17.outNote: VoteVets spent $1M for Conley before the June primary. General-election spending by named groups was not found.
NY-17.story: A district Kamala Harris won that a Republican holds. Fifth in AdImpact House spending from Aug 1 (Punchbowl, Oct 6), which says the Republican edge in bookings is partly exaggerated because Democrats buy airtime week to week.

WI-03.adBasis: spent and reserved, Aug 1 through Election Day
WI-03.outNote: AdImpact counted more than $15M from Cooke and her backers by Sept 15 (period not stated) and $3M reserved by Van Orden’s campaign alone after his Aug 11 primary (as of Aug 27). Republican groups’ amounts, and group-by-group figures on either side, were not found.
WI-03.story: Sixth in AdImpact House spending from Aug 1 (Punchbowl, Oct 6). Cooke spent heavily before her Aug 11 primary ($6.78M spent, $1.83M cash at July 22) while Van Orden held $4.68M (FEC).

KS-S.adBasis: airtime reserved for the month from Oct 2 (AdImpact via AP)
KS-S.story: Senate Leadership Fund moved money into Kansas after pulling its North Carolina ads, which AP called a pause (AP; Semafor). For the month from Oct 2, pro-Marshall advertisers had reserved about $11.0M of airtime to about $1.15M on Hamilton’s side (AdImpact via AP).

NE-S.story: No Democrat is on the ballot (Nebraska Examiner), so Osborn, an independent, faces Ricketts head to head. Dollar figures for most groups in the race were not reported; The Wall Street Journal, via Raw Story, says a new Republican super PAC has reserved more airtime than any other advertiser (AdImpact).

OH-01.outNote: House Majority PAC reserved $1.9M of TV and digital time in April for the fall (Signal Ohio). Republican-side and DCCC spending were not found.

OH-07.outNote: A new Democratic group, Affordable Ohio, spent $131,700 in one July week in the Cleveland market, the race’s first ad money (Medium Buying, via Andrew Tobias). Other spending was not found.

OH-09.outNote: House Majority PAC reserved $3M of TV and digital time in April for the fall (Signal Ohio). Congressional Leadership Fund posted about Kaptur’s ad, but no Republican-side spending figure was found.

OH-13.outNote: House Majority PAC reserved $1.175M of TV and digital time in April for the fall (Signal Ohio). Republican-side and DCCC spending were not found.
